newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds wants case dismissed, court says.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds wants case dismissed, court says.

text.p: An attorney for R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co. on Thursday asked for dismissal of the secondhand smoke lawsuit against tobacco companies, citing a U.S. Supreme Court ruling rejecting an asbestos-injury settlement, a Dade County Circuit Court spokesman said.
Reynolds attorney Hugh Whiting told Judge Robert Kaye the company intended to formally request the lawsuit be dismissed, but by early afternoon it had made no such formal filing, the spokesman said.
Whiting's statement to the judge came as jury selection continued in the case known as Norma Broin vs Philip Morris Cos Inc. et al.
There was no indication of how Kaye would respond.
On Wednesday, the U.S. Supreme Court rejected a settlement between asbestos manufacturers and about 100,000 people claiming injuries from the once widely used substance.

The justices upheld a U.S. appeals court ruling that threw out the settlement because the interests of the various plaintiffs were too diverse and too much in conflict to meet the class-action lawsuit definition under federal court rules.
